questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the Bactrian camel, consider the following statements:
1. It has two humps that store fat.
2. In India it is found in the Nubra Valley of Ladakh.
3. The wild Bactrian camel (Camelus ferus) is listed as Endangered by the IUCN.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. About 300-400 Bactrian camels are found in India. The domesticated Bactrian camel is not considered a threatened species.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to stingless bees, consider the following statements:
1. Amazon's stingless bees have become the first insect to be granted legal rights.
2. Their stingers are fully functional and are used for defence.
3. They belong to the world's oldest bee lineage, existing for nearly 80 million years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Their stingers are highly reduced and functionally useless for defence. Nearly 500 species exist globally, with over 170 in Peru, and they sustain about 80% of Amazonian flora.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to freshwater pufferfish, consider the following statements:
1. They are a group of about 30 to 35 species in the family Tetraodontidae that live their entire lives in fresh water.
2. They are found in the Western Ghats and in basins such as the Ganga, Brahmaputra and Mahanadi.
3. Their poison, tetrodotoxin, is a mild toxin of little danger to humans.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Tetrodotoxin (TTX) is one of the most potent neurotoxins known in nature. Pufferfish are omnivorous and live near the bottom. Scientists have confirmed India's first case of pufferfish poisoning.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to mycorrhizal networks, consider the following statements:
1. They are underground fungal networks that connect the roots of several plants through hyphae.
2. In the association, plants give carbohydrates to the fungi and receive better access to water and nutrients.
3. The network is popularly called the 'Wood Wide Web'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Tyler Prize, called the 'Nobel for the environment', was awarded to an American biologist for her work on these networks, which draw down about 13 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide into soil systems every year.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to bio-bitumen, consider the following statements:
1. It is made from organic materials such as agricultural waste, lignin, bio-char and bio-oil.
2. It can be used as an addition to bitumen or to reduce the amount of bitumen in the binder mixture.
3. India has become the first country to produce it commercially for road construction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It can reduce crude oil imports and help address stubble burning. Ordinary bitumen is a black, adhesive substance produced by distilling crude oil.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Biomaterials are best described as materials that are:
opts: Made from crude oil that is processed so that it can be broken down by sunlight
Derived wholly or partly from living sources or made by biological steps
Produced only from minerals found underground in the form of metals and alloys
Made from plastics that are recycled and mixed with a small fraction of metals
questions.why: They offer sustainable alternatives to traditional petroleum-based products, with applications in biomedicine, packaging, agriculture, healthcare and textiles.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to youth in India, consider the following statements:
1. National Youth Day is observed on 12 January, the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda.
2. The Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue 2026 was held in New Delhi.
3. The Agnipath Scheme recruits youth as 'Agniveers' to provide them with technical skills and discipline.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India has the largest youth population in the world, with about 50% under 25 years of age and 65% under 35. The draft National Youth Policy 2025 sets a ten-year vision.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan (VBSA) Bill, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. The VBSA will control the funding of institutions.
2. It creates a unified regulatory architecture for higher education under Entry 66 of the Union List.
3. It repeals the University Grants Commission Act, 1956, the AICTE Act, 1987 and the NCTE Act, 1993.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The VBSA will not control the funding of institutions. Legal and medical education are exempted and will continue under separate Acts. The Bill was referred to a joint parliamentary committee.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the VBSA Bill, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. Viksit Bharat Shiksha Viniyaman Parishad is the council for regulation.
2. Viksit Bharat Shiksha Gunvatta Parishad is the council for accreditation.
3. Viksit Bharat Shiksha Manak Parishad is the council for academic standards.
4. Appeals against the decisions of the Commission and the Councils lie before the Supreme Court.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: Appeals against the decisions of the Commission and the Councils lie before the Central Government. A Council of Architecture is to be set up under the Architects Act, 1972, as a professional standard-setting body.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the regulation of higher education in India, consider the following statements:
1. Education is in the Concurrent List.
2. The National Board of Accreditation accredits colleges and universities as a whole.
3. Technical and scientific institutions, research and standards are in the Union List.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The NAAC, set up by the UGC, assesses colleges and universities on quality, while the NBA, under the AICTE Act, accredits specific technical programmes such as B.Tech in Mechanical Engineering.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Supreme Court's judgment in Amit Kumar v. Union of India on student suicides, consider the following statements:
1. Vacant faculty and administrative posts must be filled within a year.
2. The Court invoked Article 142 to address the rise in student suicides in higher educational institutions.
3. Institutions must report any suicide or unnatural death to the police immediately, wherever it occurs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Vacant faculty and administrative posts must be filled within four months, with priority for reserved categories. A National Task Force is to create a framework and model SOPs for well-being audits.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Supreme Court's observation on menstrual health in schools, consider the following statements:
1. The Court held that the right to life under Article 21 includes the right to menstrual health.
2. The Court linked the matter only to Article 19 and not to Article 21A.
3. The Court directed pan-India implementation of the Menstrual Hygiene Policy for School-going Girls for Classes 6-12.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Court also linked it to Article 14 and to the right to education under Article 21A. Schools must provide gender-segregated toilets, free sanitary napkins and dedicated menstrual hygiene management corners.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: 'Demographic Winter' is best described as a phase of:
opts: A temporary fall in births that is caused only by severe cold weather in some regions
A rapid rise in the share of young people that is caused by a high fertility rate
A fall in the death rate that results in a quick increase in the working-age group
A persistent, structural fall in population growth, with fertility below replacement
questions.why: The replacement fertility rate is 2.1. China's population fell for the fourth consecutive year, by 3.39 million to 1.405 billion, with 7.92 million births in 2025.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the scramjet engine, consider the following statements:
1. It operates efficiently at hypersonic speeds above Mach 5 and allows supersonic combustion.
2. It has no mechanical compressor or turbine.
3. It can produce thrust from zero air speed without assistance from another propulsion system.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Ramjets and scramjets cannot produce thrust at zero air speed, so they need a rocket or turbojet to reach a high enough speed. India is the fourth country to demonstrate flight testing of a scramjet, after the US, Russia and China.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: A scramjet engine differs from a rocket engine in that the scramjet:
opts: Uses oxygen from the atmospheric air as the oxidiser instead of carrying its own
Carries both the fuel and the oxidiser in tanks inside the vehicle to burn in a chamber
Uses a rotating mechanical compressor and turbine to compress the incoming air flow
Works in space where there is no air, by using a gas that is stored on the vehicle
questions.why: A scramjet generally uses hydrogen as fuel. It is more efficient than a rocket, which carries both fuel and oxidiser.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the PSLV-C62 / EOS-N1 mission, consider the following statements:
1. It was a successful mission with no anomaly.
2. It was the 64th flight of the PSLV.
3. It was the ninth dedicated commercial mission of NSIL.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The mission encountered an anomaly during the third stage. NSIL, incorporated in 2019, is the commercial arm of ISRO and is wholly owned by the Government under the Department of Space.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the PSLV, consider the following statements:
1. It is a third-generation launch vehicle and the first Indian launch vehicle with liquid stages.
2. Its second stage uses the Vikas engine.
3. Its first stage uses the S139 solid rocket motor with six strap-on boosters.
4. In 2017 it launched 10 satellites in a single mission.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: In 2017 the PSLV launched 104 satellites in a single mission, a world record. It can carry up to 1,750 kg to Sun-synchronous polar orbits of 600 km.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to India's first private Earth observation constellation, consider the following statements:
1. A Pixxel-led consortium signed an agreement with IN-SPACe.
2. It is a fully government-built and government-operated infrastructure.
3. It will consist of 12 satellites, including optical, multispectral, SAR and hyperspectral imaging.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is a Public-Private Partnership, a shift from government-built to industry-operated national Earth observation infrastructure, with an investment of Rs 1,200 crore over five years. IN-SPACe is the nodal agency that authorises, regulates and promotes private participation in space.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to dark matter, consider the following statements:
1. It makes up about 68% of the universe.
2. It does not emit, absorb or reflect light.
3. Its existence is inferred from its gravitational effects on ordinary matter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Dark matter makes up about 27% of the universe and dark energy about 68%, while normal matter is about 5%. Astronomers have unveiled a detailed map of dark matter based on James Webb Space Telescope observations.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Fourth Industrial Revolution, consider the following statements:
1. The term was coined by Klaus Schwab, the founder of the World Economic Forum, in 2016.
2. The WEF centre announced for Andhra Pradesh will be the first such centre in India.
3. It describes the convergence of digital, physical and biological technologies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It will be the third such centre in India, after Mumbai and Telangana. The IMF says almost 40% of global employment is exposed to AI.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Battery Pack Aadhaar Number (BPAN), consider the following statements:
1. It is an indigenous system for end-to-end traceability of batteries through their life cycle.
2. It gives each battery pack a unique identification number.
3. It is required for all batteries, including those in small consumer products.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Draft guidelines require electric vehicle batteries and industrial batteries with capacity above 2 kWh to keep a BPAN as an electronic record. It helps second-life use and recycling.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication does not rely on third-party networks such as cellular networks.
Statement-II: V2V communication can help vehicles share warnings even when a hazard is not visible, strengthening Advanced Driver Assistance Systems.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct, but one does not explain the other. It works across the front, rear and sides of vehicles and factors in terrain and road curves.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The Mpemba effect refers to the observation that:
opts: Under certain conditions, colder substances can boil sooner than the hotter ones do
Under all conditions, ice melts at a higher temperature than the pure water freezes
Under certain conditions, hotter substances can freeze faster than colder ones
Under certain conditions, salt water freezes at a higher temperature than pure water
questions.why: It is most famously seen in water but is not limited to it. It matters for heat engines, refrigeration, quantum computing and materials science.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Nipah virus, consider the following statements:
1. It was first identified in an outbreak in India in 2018.
2. It is a zoonotic virus whose natural reservoir is fruit bats.
3. It can spread to humans through raw date palm sap or fruit contaminated by bats.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It was first identified in a 1999 outbreak in Malaysia and Singapore, in which it passed from bats to pigs to humans. The incubation period is 4 to 14 days.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to staphylococci, consider the following statements:
1. They are gram-positive cocci that occur in clusters.
2. They are viruses.
3. Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis are the main types.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: They are bacteria. Researchers found high levels of antibiotic-resistant staphylococci in indoor and outdoor air in parts of Delhi.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Somnath Temple, consider the following statements:
1. The present temple is built in the Dravida style.
2. It is located at Prabhas Patan near Veraval in Gujarat.
3. It is revered as the first among the twelve Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The present temple is in the Maru-Gurjara (Chalukya or Solanki) style. Its 'Kailash Mahameru Prasad' form has a garbhagriha, a sabhamandap and a nrityamandap, and a 150-foot shikhar.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the history of the Somnath Temple, consider the following statements:
1. Mahmud of Ghazni raided it in 1026, during the reign of Bhima I.
2. Ahilyabai Holkar rebuilt the temple in the 18th century.
3. The present temple was inaugurated by President Rajendra Prasad on 11 May 1951.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The temple was destroyed again in 1297, 1394 and 1706, and was looted as many as 17 times. Its post-independence reconstruction was initiated by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q: Which one of the following writers recorded the destruction of the Somnath temple by the army of Alauddin Khilji in the 13th century?
opts: Al-Biruni, in the Kitab-al-Hind written in the eleventh century
Kalidasa, in the Raghuvamsa written in the fifth century
Abul Fazl, in the Ain-i-Akbari written in the sixteenth century
questions.why: Al-Biruni praised the temple in the 11th century, and Kalidasa mentioned Somnath-Prabhasa as a Shiva pilgrimage site in the 5th century.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to Maru-Gurjara architecture, consider the following statements:
1. It originated in the 6th century in the regions of Rajasthan and Gujarat.
2. It reached its peak under the Chalukya (Solanki) dynasty of Gujarat.
3. A jharokha is a projecting stone window or suspended balcony.
4. A jaali is a rain-water storage tank across a slope.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: A jaali is a perforated stone or latticed screen with geometric or calligraphic patterns. A johad is a rain-water storage tank or barrier built across slopes to replenish groundwater.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Padma Awards, consider the following statements:
1. They are conferred in three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri.
2. The awards do not amount to a title under Article 18(1) and cannot be used as a prefix or suffix.
3. The number of awards is capped at 120 a year, excluding posthumous and foreigner awards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Government servants are not eligible, except doctors and scientists. The Balaji Raghavan v. Union of India (1996) judgment dealt with the status of the awards.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to gallantry awards in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Param Vir Chakra is the highest military decoration for the most conspicuous bravery.
2. The Param Vir Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra and Vir Chakra were instituted in 1952.
3. The Ashoka Chakra is the highest peacetime award for bravery away from the battlefield.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The wartime awards were instituted on 26 January 1950, and the peacetime awards on 4 January 1952, renamed in 1967 as the Ashoka Chakra, Kirti Chakra and Shaurya Chakra. They are conferred by the President.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Bhadrakali inscription, consider the following statements:
1. It is a 12th-century inscription embedded in the wall of the Bhadrakali Temple at Prabhas Patan, Gujarat.
2. It is a prashasti of Acharya Bhavabrihaspati, the spiritual preceptor of the Solanki king Kumarapala.
3. It records that the Somnath Temple was built only in stone from the beginning.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The inscription is dated to 1169 CE. It gives a legendary history of the Somnath Temple across the four Yugas, mentioning its construction in gold, silver and wood, and finally in stone by Bhimdev Solanki.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Zehanpora site in Baramulla, Kashmir, consider the following statements:
1. The finds show that Kashmir had no Buddhist heritage.
2. The stupa structures there belong to the Kushan period.
3. It lies along the ancient Silk Route to Kandahar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The discovery underscores Kashmir's Gandhara Buddhist heritage and its role as a centre of Buddhist culture and learning. Other finds include wooden superstructures, Kushan-era pottery and copper artefacts.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Bagurumba dance, consider the following statements:
1. It is a traditional folk dance of the Bodo community of Assam.
2. It is a classical dance form of Odisha.
3. It is traditionally performed by young Bodo women, with men accompanying as musicians.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is inspired by nature and symbolises blooming flowers. It is associated with festivals such as Bwisagu, the Bodo New Year, and Domasi.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
Consider the following harvest festivals and the States with which they are associated in the news:
1. Pongal : Tamil Nadu
2. Lohri : Punjab
3. Magh Bihu : Assam
4. Kanuma : Karnataka
How many of the above are correctly matched?
questions.why: Kanuma is celebrated in Telangana. Magh Bihu marks the end of the harvest season with community feasts and bonfires called Meji, and Lohri is celebrated a day before Makar Sankranti.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q: Uttarayana, known for kite flying, is a harvest festival celebrated mainly in which of the following?
questions.why: These festivals mark the change of seasons, the Sun's northward journey (Uttarayana) and the harvest of crops. Makar Sankranti marks the Sun's transition into Capricorn.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the regulation of AI on social media in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 does not apply to platforms that control AI systems.
2. The IT Act, 2000 and the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 form the backbone of social media regulation.
3. Non-compliance can lead to loss of safe harbour protection under Section 79 of the IT Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The DPDP Act, 2023 requires data fiduciaries, including platforms that control AI systems, to comply with prior consent, data protection measures and grievance redressal. The POCSO Act and the Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act make it illegal to create or share obscene material.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the governance of artificial intelligence, consider the following statements:
1. MeitY issued the India AI Governance Guidelines, which present seven sutras for ethical AI governance.
2. The EU Act allows AI practices that involve subliminal manipulation of users.
3. The EU Artificial Intelligence Act, agreed in 2024, is described as the world's first comprehensive AI law.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The EU Act categorises AI systems by risk and prohibits unacceptable-risk practices such as subliminal manipulation. OECD and UNESCO principles are non-binding but press companies to uphold fairness, transparency, privacy and human oversight.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Atal Pension Yojana (APY), consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in 2015 and is implemented by PFRDA under the National Pension System.
2. It is open to bank account holders aged 18 to 40 who are not income tax payers.
3. It guarantees a lifelong monthly pension of Rs 10,000 to Rs 25,000 from age 60.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The guaranteed monthly pension is between Rs 1,000 and Rs 5,000. The Union Cabinet approved its continuation until 2030-31, and over 8.66 crore subscribers had enrolled by 19 January 2026.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Atal Pension Yojana, consider the following statements:
1. It is a Central Sector Scheme under the Ministry of Finance.
2. On the death of the subscriber, the spouse receives the pension and the nominee receives the corpus.
3. The Government co-contribution was for subscribers who joined between 1 June 2015 and 31 March 2016.
4. A voluntary exit before age 60 returns the contribution along with the Government's co-contribution.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: On a voluntary exit the subscriber receives only the contribution with interest, and the Government co-contribution is forfeited. The co-contribution was 50% of the total contribution or Rs 1,000 a year, whichever was lower, for five years.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to PM Street Vendors AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi), consider the following statements:
1. It is a Central Sector Scheme launched in 2020 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
2. It provides collateral-free working capital loans to street vendors.
3. Street vendors are now eligible for a dedicated credit card with a limit of up to Rs 30,000.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The loan tranches are Rs 15,000, Rs 25,000 and Rs 50,000, and there is a 7% interest subsidy for timely repayment and up to Rs 1,600 in cashback for digital transactions.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The credit guarantee cover for loans under PM SVANidhi is administered by:
opts: The National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company for startups and small firms
The Small Industries Development Bank of India as its parent organisation
The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development in its rural wing
The Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises
questions.why: The scheme is implemented jointly by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and the Department of Financial Services. States must have notified rules under the Street Vendors Act, 2014.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Sanchar Saathi app, consider the following statements:
1. It was designed by the Reserve Bank of India to curb digital payment fraud.
2. The Government decided against making its pre-installation mandatory for mobile manufacturers.
3. The app has helped trace about 26 lakh stolen handsets.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The app was designed to enhance cybersecurity for citizens and help them combat cyber fraud, and it is a project of the Department of Telecommunications. It has had about 1.4 crore downloads, and the rollback was welcomed by industry for allowing stakeholder consultation.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Centre of Excellence for Financial Audit (CoEFA) launched in Hyderabad, consider the following statements:
1. It replaces the constitutional mandate of the CAG for auditing public expenditure.
2. It was launched by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
3. It will use AI and machine learning tools for technology-driven financial auditing.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It will support the CAG's constitutional mandate of ensuring transparency and accountability in public expenditure, serving as a hub for research, innovation, policy support and capacity building for auditors.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Cabinet's approval of the Census of India 2027, consider the following statements:
1. Caste data will be collected during the Houselisting phase.
2. The estimated cost is about Rs 11,718 crore.
3. Around 30 lakh field functionaries will be deployed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Cabinet decided to collect caste data electronically during the Population Enumeration phase. It will be India's first fully digital Census, with a mobile application, a self-enumeration option, a CMMS portal and the HLB Creator web-map app.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the SHANTI Bill, which received the President's assent, consider the following statements:
1. It retains the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010 unchanged.
2. It integrates the laws related to the civil nuclear sector.
3. It allows private players to participate in the civil nuclear sector with a government licence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Bill repeals both Acts. The Central Government retains exclusive rights over uranium and thorium mining, enrichment, isotopic separation, spent fuel reprocessing, high-level radioactive waste management and heavy water production.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Supreme Court's Artificial Intelligence Committee reconstituted by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, consider the following statements:
1. It is chaired by Justice P.S. Narasimha.
2. Its mandate is to guide the adoption of AI tools in the higher and subordinate judiciary.
3. The Government has already issued a formal AI policy for the judiciary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Government said that no formal AI policy or guidelines have been issued, since AI tools are in a controlled pilot phase. Concerns include algorithmic bias, language limitations, data privacy and the need for manual verification.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to DHRUVA, consider the following statements:
1. It stands for Digital Hub for Reference and Unique Virtual Address.
2. It is proposed through a draft amendment to the Post Office Act, 2023.
3. Its component DIGIPIN was rolled out in March.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. DHRUVA would allow addresses in the form 'name@entity', similar to email or UPI addresses, and private firms would be allowed to take part.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Sahakar Sarathi is a Shared Service Entity launched to modernise Rural Cooperative Banks.
Statement-II: Sahakar Sarathi has an authorised capital of Rs 1,000 crore, with NABARD, the National Cooperative Development Corporation and the participating Rural Cooperative Banks each holding 33.33%.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct, but the shareholding does not explain the purpose. It was registered on 21 July 2025 with the approval of the RBI and offers core banking solutions, AePS and UPI.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), consider the following statements:
1. Fund release does not depend on the performance of the DISCOMs.
2. The Centre has released about Rs 37,000 crore as a grant under the scheme.
3. The funds released are about 38% of the sanctioned Gross Budgetary Support.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Fund release depends on DISCOMs meeting milestones and requirements under the guidelines, and a results evaluation framework assesses the performance of States and DISCOMs.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the multi-lane free flow (MLFF) toll system, consider the following statements:
1. It is expected to be fully implemented across India by the end of 2026.
2. It lets vehicles pass through toll plazas without stopping, at speeds up to 80 km per hour.
3. It relies on satellite-based number plate recognition together with AI and FASTag.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The aim is to eliminate physical stops at toll plazas.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Asian Development Bank's loan for the Chennai Metro, consider the following statements:
1. The financing supports sections of metro lines 1 and 2 only.
2. The ADB approved a loan of US$ 240 million for the second tranche of the Chennai Metro Rail Investment Project.
3. The second tranche is part of a US$ 780 million multitranche financing facility approved in 2022.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It supports key sections of metro lines 3, 4 and 5, covering 20 km of elevated and underground corridors and 18 new stations. The first tranche was US$ 350 million.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the e-Production Investment Business Visa (e-B4 Visa), consider the following statements:
1. It is meant for tourism and leisure travel.
2. It lets foreign professionals visit India for production investment activities such as installation, commissioning and quality checks.
3. DPIIT launched an online module to generate sponsorship letters for it digitally.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is part of reforms to the business visa regime to improve ease of doing business. Activities include IT and ERP ramp-up, training, vendor empanelment and senior management visits.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Geographical Indication (GI) tag granted to Ponduru Khadi, consider the following statements:
1. The GI tag was granted by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission.
2. Ponduru Khadi is a handspun and handwoven cotton fabric from Andhra Pradesh.
3. It is made using indigenous cotton of the Srikakulam region.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The tag was granted by the Geographical Indications Registry under the Union Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The Khadi and Village Industries Commission submitted the declaration. The whole process from cleaning to weaving is manual.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGIA), consider the following statements:
1. It is the first airport in India to achieve water-positive status.
2. It has a capacity of over 40 million passengers per annum.
3. Its long-term vision is to become a net-zero airport.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Water positivity aims to reduce dependence on natural resources and improve climate resilience.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to Cyclone Ditwah, consider the following statements:
1. The name was suggested by Sri Lanka and refers to a river.
2. It brought heavy rain to Tamil Nadu and Puducherry.
3. Its name was suggested by Yemen and means 'lagoon'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The name refers to the Detwah Lagoon on Socotra Island, Yemen. Names come from a pre-approved list provided by member countries to the WMO and the UN ESCAP Panel on Tropical Cyclones.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Ramsar Convention and recent Ramsar sites, consider the following statements:
1. Siliserh Lake in Rajasthan and Kopra Jalashay in Chhattisgarh were added as India's 95th and 96th Ramsar sites.
2. The Convention was adopted in Ramsar, Iran, in 1971.
3. India acceded to the Convention in 1971.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India acceded on 1 February 1982. The Convention came into force in 1975 and is headquartered in Gland, Switzerland. Siliserh is a human-made lake built in 1845 near Alwar, in the buffer zone of the Sariska Tiger Reserve.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to India's first wildlife-safe road on NH-45, consider the following statements:
1. It was built by the Wildlife Institute of India.
2. It is in Madhya Pradesh and passes through the Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve.
3. It has 25 dedicated underpasses and an eight-foot-high fence to guide animals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It was launched by the National Highways Authority of India as part of its Green Highways initiative. Table-top red markings alert drivers to danger zones and encourage lower speeds.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the World Bank's financing for clean air programmes in Uttar Pradesh and Haryana, consider the following statements:
1. The Uttar Pradesh Clean Air Management Programme was approved with US$ 299.66 million.
2. The programmes are the first in which Indian States use airshed-based and multi-sectoral approaches.
3. The Uttar Pradesh programme aims to provide clean cooking access to 3.9 million households.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The World Bank said the programmes would help both States become more attractive business destinations while improving quality of life.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to India's first indigenous hydrogen fuel-cell vessel, consider the following statements:
1. It is powered by diesel engines with a hydrogen additive.
2. It was flagged off in Varanasi.
3. Its commercial operations were inaugurated at Namo Ghat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It runs on a hydrogen fuel cell. India joins China, Norway, the Netherlands and Japan in operating hydrogen-powered vessels. It is part of the modernisation of inland waterways.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, consider the following statements:
1. The List does not include any living traditions.
2. Deepavali was inscribed on the List in 2025.
3. India now has 15 elements on the List.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The List includes living traditions, skills and expressions passed down the generations, such as oral traditions, performing arts, festivals and traditional craftsmanship. India's elements include Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja, Garba, yoga, Vedic chanting and Ramlila, and India has nominated Chhath Puja for the next cycle.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Gyan Bharatam Mission, consider the following statements:
1. It is a mission of the Ministry of Education to promote school textbooks.
2. It is a flagship initiative of the Ministry of Culture to preserve ancient Indian knowledge systems.
3. The University of Patanjali was named India's first Yoga and Ayurveda-focused cluster centre under it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Mission works through research, digitisation and institutional mentoring, mainly of manuscripts. Thirty-three MoUs have been signed, including 20 cluster centres.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Hornbill Festival, consider the following statements:
1. It is held at the Kisama Heritage Village in Nagaland.
2. The festival showcases the cultural heritage of Nagaland's 17 tribes.
3. Switzerland, Ireland and the United Kingdom joined as official Partner Countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Angami stone-pulling ceremony symbolises unity within Naga society.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India-Afghanistan relations, consider the following statements:
1. India has formally recognised the Taliban regime.
2. India is set to restart air cargo services with Afghanistan, with air freight corridors between Kabul and Delhi and Amritsar.
3. The two sides plan to post trade attachés in each other's embassies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India has increased pragmatic engagement without formally recognising the Taliban. The inactive joint working group on trade is to be revived, and India's embassy in Kabul has been reopened.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: India was re-elected to the Council of the International Maritime Organisation for 2026-27 in which category?
opts: The ten States with the largest interest in providing international shipping services
The ten States with the largest interest in international seaborne trade
Twenty States chosen to ensure representation of all the geographical areas
The ten States with the largest number of ships registered under their flags
questions.why: India received 154 of 169 valid votes, the highest tally in its category, at the 34th session of the IMO Assembly in London.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the 'Leading Container Ports of the World' report by DNV and Menon Economics, consider the following statements:
1. It is the first edition of the report.
2. Singapore is ranked as the top container port.
3. Shanghai remains the busiest port in the world, with 51.5 million TEUs in 2024.
4. Singapore led only one of the five pillars of the index.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: Singapore led all five pillars: enablers, connectivity and customer value, productivity, sustainability, and overall impact. The next four in the top five are Shanghai, Ningbo-Zhoushan, Rotterdam and Busan.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the 'New G20' announced by the United States for 2026, consider the following statements:
1. South Africa has been invited to participate as the host of the previous presidency.
2. The United States will host the 2026 G20 Leaders' Summit in Miami.
3. Poland is welcomed as a new participant.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: South Africa has been excluded for the time being. The themes are removing regulatory burdens, unlocking affordable and secure energy supply chains, and pioneering technologies such as AI. The summit coincides with America's 250th anniversary.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the UNESCO Global Network of Learning Cities, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched by the UNESCO Institute for Lifelong Learning in 2013.
2. UNESCO added 72 new cities from 46 countries, taking the total number of cities in the network to 425.
3. UNESCO has its headquarters in Geneva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: UNESCO is headquartered in Paris, was established in 1945 and has 194 member states. The new intake includes 11 capital cities, such as Cairo, Riyadh, Lisbon, Ankara, Hanoi and Buenos Aires.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India's resolution on 'Strengthening the Global Management of Wildfires' was adopted at the 7th session of the United Nations Environment Assembly in Nairobi.
Statement-II: India warned, citing a UNEP report, that wildfires could rise by 14% by 2030, 30% by 2050 and 50% by 2100 if trends continue.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct, but the projections are a warning in the speech rather than an explanation of the adoption. The resolution calls for stronger international cooperation, early warning systems and satellite and ground-based monitoring.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to Italy's recognition by UNESCO in December 2025, consider the following statements:
1. Italy became the first country to have its entire national cuisine recognised by UNESCO.
2. Earlier recognitions were given to whole national cuisines, not to individual dishes.
3. The cuisine was added to the Intangible Cultural Heritage List.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Earlier recognitions were for individual dishes or food traditions. The announcement came during UNESCO's cultural assembly held in Delhi.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the recent presidential election in Chile, consider the following statements:
1. His victory marks a shift to the left in Chilean politics.
2. José Antonio Kast was elected the 38th President of Chile.
3. He won over 58% of the vote against Jeanette Jara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is a significant shift to the right since 1990, after a campaign on security, immigration and crime, in line with a trend in Argentina, Ecuador, Costa Rica and El Salvador.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India's chairmanship of BRICS, consider the following statements:
1. Brazil handed the BRICS presidency to India at the 4th BRICS Sherpas Meeting in Brasilia.
2. India officially assumed the chairmanship on 1 January 2026.
3. The BRICS has expanded to 11 members under Brazil's 2025 presidency.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Brazil's presidency issued the Rio Declaration with 126 commitments and approved the first Climate Finance Framework. The Amazonian wooden gavel symbolised environmental consciousness.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the GI tags recently granted to products from the States, consider the following statements:
1. The Arunachal Pradesh 'dao', a traditional handcrafted blade, received a GI tag.
2. The Darjeeling Mandarin Orange received a GI tag in November 2025.
3. The Darjeeling Organic Farmers Producer Organisation is the registered proprietor of the Darjeeling Mandarin Orange GI tag.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Arunachal Pradesh has 20 GI tags and aims to reach 50 by 2030, including the Wakro Orange and Idu Mishmi textiles. The Darjeeling Mandarin has been affected by virus and pest issues over 15 years.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, consider the following statements:
1. Rajasthan became the first State to fully digitise its 5.46 crore voter rolls under SIR.
2. SIR is a programme of the State Governments to update their voter lists.
3. The exercise used ECINET, the BLO app and portal verification.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: SIR is a nationwide programme of the Election Commission of India to update, verify and correct voter lists, remove duplicates, enrol new voters and ensure accurate polling-station mapping.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Chhattisgarh Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) (Second) Bill, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. It aims to decriminalise minor offences by replacing prison terms with fines.
2. It aims to amend 116 provisions across 14 Acts.
3. Chhattisgarh is the first State to propose a second edition of the Jan Vishwas Bill.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It focuses on trust-based governance and a lighter burden on the courts, and other States such as Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Tripura, Gujarat, Haryana and Odisha are advancing similar laws.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSG: MBY), consider the following statements:
1. It is meant only for industrial and commercial consumers.
2. It is a demand-driven scheme for rooftop solar systems for residential consumers with grid-connected electricity.
3. Consumers apply through the National Portal of the scheme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: As of 26 November 2025, 18,72,499 rooftop solar systems had been installed, benefitting 23,47,694 households. Karnataka had 14,151 systems benefitting 22,313 households.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the Pavagada Solar Park, consider the following statements:
1. It is in Karnataka.
2. It has a capacity of 2,000 MW.
3. It has been fully operational since December 2019.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Rs 351.94 crore of Central Financial Assistance has been released for the park and its power evacuation infrastructure. Karnataka had 25,675 MW of renewable capacity, about 10.24% of the national total, on 31 October 2025.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the 'smart blue harbours' initiative, consider the following statements:
1. It is led by the Department of Fisheries together with the Food and Agriculture Organisation of the UN.
2. It is financed entirely by the Ministry of Shipping.
3. Pilot projects are planned at Jakhau in Gujarat, Vanakbara in Diu and Karaikal in Puducherry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana has allocated Rs 452.32 crore for integrated fisheries infrastructure. The Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying leads the initiative.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to Madhya Pradesh's tiger corridor, consider the following statements:
1. It is to be India's first State-level multi-national-park tiger corridor.
2. It is being developed with NHAI and the PWD.
3. It has no underpasses, as animals cross roads at grade.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The corridor will integrate underpasses in forest areas, slow-traffic zones and wildlife-safe designs. It aims to promote eco-tourism while balancing tiger movement and local connectivity.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Konark Festival and the International Sand Art Festival in Odisha, consider the following statements:
1. The 36th Konark Festival and the 15th International Sand Art Festival were inaugurated together.
2. They run for five days.
3. They are organised by the Tourism Department, Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi and the Odisha Tourism Development Corporation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The inaugural evening featured an Odissi performance by Sonali Mohapatra and artists from Nrutya Upasana Pitha, Bhubaneswar.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to foreign direct investment (FDI) in India in April-September 2025-26, consider the following statements:
1. Net FDI more than doubled to $7.64 billion from $3.4 billion a year earlier.
2. Gross FDI inflows rose by 16.14% to $50.36 billion.
3. Outward FDI by Indian firms rose to $16.32 billion.
4. Net FDI was positive in September 2025.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: Net FDI was negative at $2.37 billion in September 2025, worse than the negative $1.17 billion in September 2024. Net FDI is inflows minus outflows.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to forecasts of India's growth for 2025-26, consider the following statements:
1. Crisil raised its forecast of GDP growth to 7% from 6.5%.
2. Both agencies said that exports were the main driver of growth.
3. Fitch raised its forecast to 7.4% from 6.9%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Both identified private consumption as the main driver, helped by GST reforms, income tax cuts and repo rate cuts. India grew 8.2% in Q2 of FY26, despite effective US tariffs of around 35% on exports.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the National Strategy for Financial Inclusion (NSFI): 2025-30, consider the following statements:
1. It is a strategy of the Ministry of Finance with no role for the RBI.
2. It was announced by the RBI Governor.
3. It has five key objectives known as 'Panch-Jyoti' and 47 action points.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It uses a synergistic ecosystem approach to improve last-mile access and use of financial services, and it was developed with input from government departments and financial regulators.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), consider the following statements:
1. SBI, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank continue to be identified as D-SIBs.
2. SBI has an additional Common Equity Tier 1 requirement of 0.80% of risk-weighted assets.
3. The indicators for identifying a D-SIB include size, interconnectedness, substitutability and complexity.
4. D-SIBs are not required to maintain any extra capital over the capital conservation buffer.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: D-SIBs must keep additional CET1 over the capital conservation buffer. HDFC Bank has 0.40% and ICICI Bank 0.20%. D-SIBs are perceived as too big to fail.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Government's disinvestment through Offers for Sale (OFS), consider the following statements:
1. The Government plans to sell up to 6% in Bank of Maharashtra and up to 3% in Indian Overseas Bank.
2. The Government held only 40% of Bank of Maharashtra before the sale.
3. SEBI norms require all listed companies, including public sector ones, to have a minimum public shareholding of 25%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Government held 79.60% of Bank of Maharashtra and 94.61% of Indian Overseas Bank. The sale would bring its holding in Bank of Maharashtra below 75%.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Startup India initiative, consider the following statements:
1. The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups is operated by SIDBI.
2. DPIIT had recognised 1,97,692 startups as of 31 October 2025.
3. The Fund of Funds for Startups has a corpus of Rs 10,000 crore and is operated by SIDBI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups is operated by the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company and has been in force since 1 April 2023. The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme has a corpus of Rs 945 crore and has been implemented since 1 April 2021.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the RBI's liquidity operations, consider the following statements:
1. The RBI announced open market operation purchases of Rs 1 trillion of government securities.
2. Open market operations reduce bank reserves.
3. The RBI also announced a $5 billion dollar-rupee swap to inject durable liquidity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Open market purchases of securities increase bank reserves, lower short-term interest rates and support smooth monetary transmission. The measures came as the rupee weakened past 90 per dollar amid foreign outflows.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Past Risk and Return Verification Agency (PaRRVA) launched by SEBI, consider the following statements:
1. It independently verifies the past returns of SEBI-registered market intermediaries.
2. A recognised stock exchange acts as the PaRRVA Data Centre.
3. A SEBI-registered credit rating agency serves as the verifier.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The framework covers Investment Advisers, Research Analysts and stockbrokers offering algorithmic trading, and aims to counter inflated claims by 'finfluencers'.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Indian Digital Payment Intelligence Corporation (IDPIC), consider the following statements:
1. SBI and Bank of Baroda received RBI approval to set it up.
2. It will be a Section 8 non-profit company under the Companies Act, 2013.
3. It will detect and prevent fraud in digital transactions within public sector banks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The approval depends on an exemption from the Ministry of Finance that lets the banks hold over 30% of its paid-up share capital until 16 October 2026, under Section 19(2) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Bill, consider the following statements:
1. It raises the FDI limit in insurance from 74% to 100%.
2. It amends the Insurance Act, 1938, the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956 and the IRDAI Act, 1999.
3. It allows foreign nationals to head Indian insurance companies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The top leadership of insurance companies must be Indian citizens. The Bill also lets the IRDAI demand disgorgement of wrongful gains from insurers and intermediaries and allows mergers between non-insurance and insurance firms.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the risk-based deposit insurance framework approved by the RBI's Central Board, consider the following statements:
1. The present system charges a flat premium of 12 paise per Rs 100 of assessable deposits.
2. Sound banks will pay a higher premium than less sound banks.
3. Insurance coverage is limited to Rs 5 lakh per depositor per bank.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Sound banks are expected to pay a lower premium, while less sound banks may pay 12 or up to 15 paise. The DICGC Act allows the premium to go up to 15 paise per Rs 100 with RBI approval.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The coal gasification joint venture of BPCL and Coal India, at Chandrapur in Maharashtra, aims to produce which one of the following?
opts: Synthetic natural gas as an indigenous alternative to imported natural gas
Compressed natural gas for the vehicles that are used in the cities of the State
Green hydrogen that is produced by splitting water with the help of renewable power
Petroleum coke that is used as a fuel in the cement plants of the nearby areas
questions.why: Coal India holds 51% and BPCL 49% of the joint venture, which will operate at the Western Coalfields. The Coal Ministry approved an incentive scheme of Rs 8,500 crore in January 2025 for gasification projects.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to Japan's MUFG Bank's investment in Shriram Finance, consider the following statements:
1. MUFG gets the right to appoint all the directors of the board of Shriram Finance.
2. MUFG acquired a 20% stake for about Rs 39,600 crore through preferential allotment.
3. It is described as the largest foreign direct investment in India's financial sector.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: MUFG gets the right to appoint two nominee directors. The floor price was Rs 840.83 per share, and MUFG acquired 47.11 crore equity shares.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the ADB's loan to Mizoram for strengthening public healthcare, consider the following statements:
1. The loan is a US$ 108 million results-based loan.
2. The scheme offers coverage of up to Rs 50,000 per family each year.
3. It supports the rollout of a new health insurance umbrella scheme that integrates the PM Jan Arogya Yojana with the State scheme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The scheme offers coverage of up to Rs 5,00,000 per family annually, on a single cashless and paperless platform. Mizoram is the first State to undertake this type of reform with ADB support.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to UPI biometric authentication launched by Amazon Pay, consider the following statements:
1. The feature was launched in violation of NPCI guidelines.
2. It allows PIN-free transactions of up to Rs 5,000 using fingerprint or face recognition on Android devices.
3. The biometric data stays on the device.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Amazon Pay says it follows NPCI guidelines. The rollout began on 16 December 2025.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the voluntary amalgamation of two co-operative banks in Gujarat approved by the RBI, consider the following statements:
1. The scheme was sanctioned under Section 44A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
2. Both schemes came into effect on 15 December 2025.
3. All branches of Amod Nagric Co-operative Bank operate as branches of Bhuj Mercantile Co-operative Bank.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The second amalgamation was between Amarnath Co-operative Bank and Kalupur Commercial Co-operative Bank.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the quantum sensing facilities at IIT Bombay inaugurated recently, consider the following statements:
1. QMagPI is described as India's first portable magnetometer able to detect ultra-low magnetic fields.
2. The Liquid Helium facility is meant to raise the cost of cryogenic experiments in India.
3. It was developed using nitrogen vacancy centres in diamond.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The facility is meant to reduce the cost of cryogenic experiments and build indigenous cryogenic capacity for quantum computing. The Quantum Diamond Microscope images magnetic fields at the nanoscale.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The Infinity Campus inaugurated by the Prime Minister is a rocket manufacturing facility of which one of the following startups?
questions.why: Skyroot Aerospace of Hyderabad built the 2-lakh sq ft campus, which can build one orbital rocket a month. Its first orbital rocket is Vikram-I.
questions.insight: Skyroot's sub-orbital rocket Vikram-S made it the first Indian private company to launch a rocket to space in 2022.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to Skyroot Aerospace, consider the following:
1. It launched Vikram-S, a sub-orbital rocket, in 2022.
2. Its Infinity Campus is located in Hyderabad.
3. Its founders are former ISRO scientists.
4. Vikram-I is its first sub-orbital rocket.
How many of the above of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: Vikram-I is its first orbital rocket, able to put satellites in orbit. The founders are Pawan Chandana and Bharath Dhaka.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The National Coral Reef Research Institute (NCRRI) is to be set up at which one of the following places?
opts: Port Blair in the Nicobar district
Gulf of Mannar in Tamil Nadu
questions.why: The Environment Ministry will set it up at Chidiyatapu at an estimated cost of Rs 120 crore, as the nodal agency for coral reef research across India.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Vessel Traffic Management System (VTMS) developed in India, consider the following statements:
1. It was developed by IIT Madras through the National Technology Centre for Ports, Waterways and Coasts.
2. It provides vessel position tracking and meteorological hazard warnings.
3. It was developed for the Ministry of Defence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It was developed on requirements set by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, which allocated Rs 10 crore to IIT Madras in 2020 for the software.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the discovery of the spiral galaxy 'Alaknanda' by Indian astronomers, consider the following statements:
1. It is a grand-design spiral galaxy seen as it existed about 12 billion years ago.
2. Its structure agrees with older models that predicted early galaxies to be chaotic.
3. The James Webb Space Telescope and gravitational lensing by the cluster Abell 2744 helped observe it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It defies older models that predicted chaotic and irregular early galaxies. It spans about 30,000 light-years and forms stars at a rate much higher than the Milky Way's present rate.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the DHRUV64 microprocessor, consider the following statements:
1. It is a 1.0 GHz, 64-bit dual-core processor.
2. It was developed by C-DAC under the Microprocessor Development Programme.
3. It is suitable for 5G infrastructure, automotive systems and IoT.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It is described as India's first fully indigenous processor of this type and supports the India Semiconductor Mission's aim of self-reliance.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The first AI-driven community screening programme in India for diabetic retinopathy has been launched by which one of the following?
questions.why: The AFMS launched it with AIIMS and the e-Health AI Unit of the Health Ministry. The pilot runs at seven locations including Pune, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Dharamshala, Gaya, Jorhat and Kochi.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Indian Navy commissioned INS Mahe, the first vessel of the Mahe-class anti-submarine warfare shallow water craft.
Statement-II: INS Mahe was built by Cochin Shipyard Limited as part of the Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both statements are correct. The second gives the builder and the policy setting, but it does not explain the commissioning. The craft is suited to littoral waters, coastal patrols and securing sea routes.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to joint military exercises of India in December 2025, consider the following:
1. EKUVERIN with the Maldives National Defence Force
2. Suryakiran with Nepal
3. Desert Cyclone with the UAE
4. AviaIndra with Russia
How many of the above of the above exercises were hosted by India?
questions.why: Ekuverin XIV was held at Thiruvananthapuram, Suryakiran XIX at Pithoragarh and AviaIndra-2025 was hosted by the Indian Air Force. Desert Cyclone-II was held in Abu Dhabi, so India sent its contingent there.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Indo-Pacific Logistics Network Field Training Exercise held in December 2025, consider the following statements:
1. It was the first such exercise and no Quad tabletop exercise had been held earlier.
2. It was conducted by the Quad partners Australia, India, Japan and the US.
3. It took place at Andersen Air Force Base in Guam alongside Operation Christmas Drop.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: A Tabletop Exercise had been held in April 2025. The field exercise aimed to improve shared logistics capacity for humanitarian and disaster response in the Indo-Pacific.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the BrahMos missile, consider the following statements:
1. BrahMos Aerospace is a joint venture of DRDO and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyenia.
2. It is a subsonic cruise missile.
3. The missile is named after the rivers Brahmaputra and Moskva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile. Its first successful test was on 12 June 2001 at the Integrated Test Range off Odisha, and the recent launch was from the Southern Command in the Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the fighter aircraft escape system test conducted by DRDO, consider the following statements:
1. It was conducted at the Rail Track Rocket Sled facility at Chandigarh.
2. ADA and HAL collaborated with DRDO in the test.
3. It used a dual-sled system with a Tejas (LCA) forebody and an instrumented dummy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The test, with phased rocket motor firings to reach precise velocities, places India among the few countries able to test such systems.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Border Roads Organisation (BRO), consider the following statements:
1. BRO's expenditure in 2024-25 was below Rs 10,000 crore.
2. The Defence Minister inaugurated 125 BRO projects together, the most simultaneous inaugurations by it.
3. The Shyok Tunnel, 920 metres long, is among the projects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: BRO's expenditure reached a record Rs 16,690 crore in 2024-25, with a target of Rs 18,700 crore for 2025-26. The projects cost about Rs 5,000 crore and include 28 roads and 93 bridges.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Chief Information Commissioner (CIC), consider the following statements:
1. The President appoints the CIC on the recommendation of a committee.
2. The Chief Justice of India is a member of the committee.
3. The committee consists of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Chief Justice is not a member. Raj Kumar Goyal, a 1990-batch IAS officer, was sworn in as CIC on 15 December 2025, succeeding Heeralal Samariya.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Justice Surya Kant, who took oath as the 53rd Chief Justice of India, is due to retire on which one of the following dates?
questions.why: He was born on 10 February 1962 and retires at 65, on 9 February 2027, which gives a tenure of nearly 15 months after succeeding Justice B R Gavai.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the COP30 climate summit at Belem, consider the following statements:
1. The final decision called for developed countries to triple adaptation finance by 2035.
2. The final agreement did not mention a phase-out of fossil fuels.
3. The United States sent an official delegation led by a Cabinet Secretary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The United States did not send an official delegation. The COP30 presidency said it would issue separate documents on the fossil fuel transition and forest protection outside the official agreement.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit, consider the following statements:
1. The summit marked 25 years of the Strategic Partnership that began in 2000.
2. The leaders adopted Programme 2030 to deepen cooperation in trade, technology, defence and energy.
3. It reaffirmed a Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Annual Summit is the highest-level institutional dialogue between the two countries.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q: The Intergovernmental Committee for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage meets under which one of the following UNESCO instruments?
questions.why: It has 24 members elected for four years, with half rotating every two years. Its 20th session was held at the Red Fort in New Delhi, where Deepavali was inscribed on the Representative List.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the UNESCO Intergovernmental Committee for Safeguarding of Intangible Cultural Heritage, consider the following:
1. It has 24 members.
2. Members are elected for four years.
3. Members can be re-elected for consecutive terms.
4. It reviews nominations to the Representative List.
How many of the above of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: Consecutive terms are not allowed, which ensures wide participation. Half the members rotate every two years.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The India-AI Impact Summit 2026 makes India the first country of which one of the following to hold a global AI summit?
questions.why: It is scheduled in New Delhi from 16 to 20 February, after summits in the UK and Paris, and has seven themes called 'Chakras'.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Second WHO Global Summit on Traditional Medicine held in New Delhi in December 2025, consider the following statements:
1. It was co-hosted by the WHO and the Ministry of Ayush.
2. It was attended only by Ayush practitioners from South Asia.
3. Its theme was 'Restoring balance: The science and practice of health and well-being'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It brought together policymakers, scientists, practitioners, Indigenous knowledge holders and civil society from over 100 countries.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Annual Ground Water Quality Report 2025, consider the following statements:
1. It found that more than half of all samples had uranium contamination.
2. It was released by the Central Ground Water Board under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
3. It is based on about 15,000 samples collected in 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The report found 13 to 15 per cent of samples had uranium above limits. Most groundwater in India is safe, but some regions face rising uranium levels.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the NITI Aayog report 'Deepening the Corporate Bond Market in India', consider the following statements:
1. It says the market is limited by thin depth and a concentrated investor profile.
2. It recommends that bond issuance be limited to the banking sector.
3. It recommends more issuance by mid-size firms and wider participation of insurance and pension funds.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It wants to reduce reliance on bank credit. It also suggests credit enhancement, long-tenor and sustainability-linked bonds and tokenised bonds.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Stanford Global AI Vibrancy rankings 2025, consider the following statements:
1. India improved its rank in policy and governance.
2. India ranks third, behind the United States and China.
3. India climbed four places from seventh in 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India slipped five places in policy and governance, which is an area needing attention. The index uses seven pillars including R&D, talent and infrastructure.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: In the Arton Capital Passport Index 2025, which one of the following countries has the strongest passport for the seventh consecutive year?
questions.why: The UAE has a Mobility Score of 179. Singapore and Spain share second place at 175, and India ranks 67th with a score of 74.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to the observance of Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) in India, consider the following statements:
1. It commemorates the adoption of the Constitution on 26 November 1949.
2. The Government of India began observing it in 2015.
3. Before 2015, 26 November was observed as Law Day.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Government declared the day in 2015, the year of the 125th birth anniversary of Dr B R Ambedkar, to promote constitutional values.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to the Constitution of India, consider the following:
1. The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949.
2. Constitution Day has been observed since 2015.
3. The day was observed as Law Day before 2015.
4. The Constitution came into force on 26 November 1949.
How many of the above of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 but came into force on 26 January 1950, which is why Republic Day is observed on 26 January.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to the Indian Navy's Operation Trident of December 1971, consider the following statements:
1. It is the event commemorated by Navy Day on 4 December.
2. It was carried out in the Bay of Bengal against East Pakistan's ports.
3. The Navy sank four Pakistani vessels, including PNS Khaibar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The attack was on the Pakistani Navy's base at Karachi in the Arabian Sea. Navy Day 2025 was marked with an operational demonstration at Shangumugham beach in Thiruvananthapuram.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Navy Day is observed on 4 December in India to commemorate which one of the following events?
opts: The mutiny of the Royal Indian Navy in 1946
The liberation of Goa through Operation Vijay
The commissioning of INS Vikrant in 1961
questions.why: On 4 December 1971 the Navy sank four Pakistani vessels including PNS Khaibar in Operation Trident during the war that led to Bangladesh.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to the cooperative dairy movement in India, consider the following statements:
1. Dr Verghese Kurien is called the Father of the White Revolution.
2. National Milk Day is observed on 26 November on his birth anniversary.
3. Operation Flood was completed in a single phase between 1970 and 1975.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Operation Flood was developed in three phases: 1970-80, 1981-85 and 1985-96. The Anand model was taken nationwide on the orders of Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri. India now provides about 25 per cent of global milk production.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to the mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan, consider the following statements:
1. He was born in Erode, Tamil Nadu, on 22 December 1887.
2. He was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society of London in 1918.
3. National Mathematics Day on 22 December was designated by the Government of India in 2012.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. His first paper was published in 1911 in the Journal of the Indian Mathematical Society, and he got a degree by research from Cambridge in 1916.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Government of India observes 22 December as National Mathematics Day.
Statement-II: Srinivasa Ramanujan was born on 22 December 1887.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct and the birth anniversary of Ramanujan is the reason for the observance, which was designated in 2012.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Ram Sutar, who passed away recently, is best known for designing which one of the following monuments?
questions.why: Sutar designed the Statue of Unity in Gujarat honouring Sardar Patel. He also made the Parliament premises statues of Mahatma Gandhi meditating and Shivaji on horseback.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
